prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Checkout A/B Test Results (language en).
Grid: 7 columns × 9 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Metric" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Control" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Variant" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Lift" spans 1 col × 2 row; "p-value" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Metric" · longest unbreakable word 88px · one-line width 232px
  col 2: header "Control › Mean" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 46px
  col 3: header "Control › 95% CI" · longest unbreakable word 52px · one-line width 100px
  col 4: header "Variant › Mean" · longest unbreakable word 43px · one-line width 44px
  col 5: header "Variant › 95% CI" · longest unbreakable word 52px · one-line width 97px
  col 6: header "Lift" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 46px
  col 7: header "p-value" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 48px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 674px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 673px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 674px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Compare checkout metrics between control and variant, including estimated lift, uncertainty, and statistical significance.","reading":"Readers scan metric names down the first column, then compare the two means and confidence intervals across each row before checking lift and p-value. Wrapped labels should remain visually connected to their values.","groups":["Control and Variant each pair a mean with a 95% confidence interval; matching subcolumns support comparison between the two groups.","Lift and p-value summarize the comparison and should remain easy to scan alongside the group results."],"keep_intact":["Individual numbers, percentages, currency amounts, time values, and p-values.","Confidence interval ranges where possible, especially time and currency ranges.","Short column headers and metric identifiers such as 7-day and 1,000."],"may_wrap":["Long metric names at word boundaries, especially Support contacts per 1,000 sessions.","Confidence intervals at natural break points if space is prioritized for metric names; affected rows will become taller.","The two-level Control and Variant headers already occupy two header rows."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[166,67,121,65,118,67,69],"idea":"Keep the measured values and confidence intervals on one line, allowing longer metric names to wrap."},{"name":"B","widths":[210,65,100,64,100,66,68],"idea":"Give metric names more room while accepting wraps in the longest confidence intervals."},{"name":"C","widths":[140,70,120,70,120,76,77],"idea":"Use closely matched widths for Control and Variant and generous summary columns, with a narrow metric column and nearly full-width confidence intervals."}]}
